privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: How Levantine Express Ltd collects, uses and protects your personal data when you use our services.

blocks.title: Key points
items: Levantine Express Ltd is the data controller for your data.
We keep your data only as long as we need it, or until you ask us to delete it.
You can ask to see, correct or delete your data at any time.
You can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO).

blocks.title: Who we are
blocks.body: Levantine Express Ltd is registered in England and Wales (company no. 11630563). We decide why and how your data is processed, which makes us the data controller under UK GDPR.

blocks.title: What this policy covers
blocks.body: This policy covers how we and our users handle data on our services. It doesn’t cover third-party websites we link to, including social media.

blocks.title: Data we collect
items: Data you give us when you contact us by app, website, phone, post or email.
Data collected automatically, such as your IP address, when and how often you visit, and how you use our content. We use it to improve our services.

blocks.title: How we keep it safe
blocks.body: Accounts are password-protected and personal to you, and data is stored on secure servers. If you think your data has been misused, lost or accessed without permission, email us:

blocks.title: How long we keep it
blocks.body: We keep your data only as long as we need it for the purposes in this policy, or until you ask us to delete it, unless the law requires us to keep it longer. Deleted data may stay on backups for legal, tax or regulatory reasons.

blocks.title: Your rights
items: Access
See the data we hold about you, usually free of charge.
Correction
Fix anything that’s wrong or incomplete.
Erasure
Ask us to delete your data.
Restriction

blocks.body: If the business is sold or restructured, your data may move to the new owner and be used for the same purposes. We’ll take steps to protect your privacy.

blocks.title: Changes to this policy
blocks.body: We may update this policy when needed or when the law requires it. Using our services after a change means you accept the updated policy.

blocks.body: This policy is governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.

fraud.title: Fraud Warning
fraud.intro: Scammers use fake websites, texts and calls that look genuine to steal your money or personal information. Here’s how to stay safe.

blocks.text: The police, your bank and HMRC will never cold call you to ask for your bank details.

blocks.title: Do
items: Use a strong, different password for every account.
Research unfamiliar companies before you buy.
Turn down unsolicited offers and deals that seem too good to be true.
Keep records of online purchases, like receipts and order confirmations.
Contact your bank straight away if money goes missing.
Report scams to the police and to Action Fraud.

blocks.title: Don’t
items: Share personal information with callers you don’t know.
Click links in suspicious emails or texts.
Reuse passwords, especially for accounts linked to your bank.
Give personal details to people who turn up unannounced.
Rush into decisions when someone pressures you.
Keep quiet if you think you’ve been scammed.
blocks.note: If you’re unsure, ask a friend or relative for advice.

blocks.title: Warning signs
items: A greeting that’s impersonal, or uses the wrong name or title.
A sender address that doesn’t match the company’s real domain.
Links in messages about problems with your account. Go to the company’s website yourself instead.
Pop-ups asking for personal details. Close them without typing anything.
Websites without a padlock or https:// in the address.

blocks.title: Common scams
items: Fake offers and free trials
Bogus offers and fake goods that take your money or card details.
Copycat government websites
Fake sites that copy official services like HMRC and charge you to renew passports or visas.
Dating and romance scams
People you meet online who ask for money. Never send them money or let them pay money into your account.
Holiday fraud
Holidays or accommodation that don’t exist, often found out only on arrival.
Mandate fraud
A hacked or copied email changes the bank details on a genuine invoice, so your payment goes to the scammer.
Pharming
You’re sent to a fake website even when you type the right address.
Phishing
Messages pretending to be your bank, HMRC or PayPal that lead to a fake login page.

blocks.title: If you think you’ve been scammed
items: Contact your bank or card provider straight away.
Report it to the police.
Report it to Action Fraud.
